text: Welcome to this demo. In some voice experiences, silence is not a mistake. Silence is the time the user needs to do the thing they were just asked to do. If the voice keeps talking too quickly, the task becomes impossible. In a math learning app, the tutor says, now it's your turn. What is 2 plus 3? The answer is 5. Then the tutor says, try another one. You have 6 apples. You give 2 away, and then you get 3 more. How many apples do you have now? You have 7 apples. The useful moment is the space between the question and the answer, because the learner needs time to calculate. In a language learning app, the teacher says, repeat after me in Spanish. Hello. Hola. Good morning. Buenos dias. Thank you. Gracias. Then the teacher changes the task and says, now I'll say the English word, and you say the Spanish word before I tell you. Hello. Hola. Thank you. Gracias. The silence matters because the learner needs time to speak. In a fitness app, the coach says, squat down and hold. Stand up. Step your right foot back into a lunge and hold there. Return to standing. In a breathing app, the guide says, breathe in slowly. Hold your breath. Breathe out slowly. These instructions only work if the user has time to move or breathe before hearing the next step. In a journaling app, the guide says, think of one thing that made today difficult. Now write one sentence about it. Think of one thing that helped you get through it. Write that down too. In a visual search app, the voice says, look at the picture and find the red triangle. Now tap it. Find the smallest circle. Now tap that. End of demo. The voice should pause whenever the user needs to think, answer, move, speak, write, search, choose, calculate, or act.
